questions.problem:
Given that the discrete random variable $Y$ has the probability mass function $f(y)$ and the cumulative distribution function $F(y)$ as shown in the table below, compute $a+b+c.$

| $y$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(y)$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ | $0.2$ | $0.4$ | $0.1$ |
| $F(y)$ | $0.1$ | $a$ | $0.5$ | $b$ | $c$ |
questions.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable $Y$ is a function $F(y)$ such that

$$
F(y)=P(Y\le y).
$$

Computing $a,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =F(1) \\  & =P(Y\le 1) \\  & =P(Y\in {0,1}) \\  & =f(0)+f(1) \\  & =0.1+0.2 \\  & =0.3.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $b,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}b & =F(3) \\  & =P(Y\le 3) \\  & =P(Y\in {0,1,2,3}) \\  & =f(0)+f(1)+f(2)+f(3) \\  & =0.1+0.2+0.2+0.4 \\  & =0.9.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $c,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =F(4) \\  & =P(Y\le 4) \\  & =P(Y\in {0,1,2,3,4}) \\  & =f(0)+f(1)+f(2)+f(3)+f(4) \\  & =0.1+0.2+0.2+0.4+0.1 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
a+b+c=0.3+0.9+1=2.2.
$$

questions.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable $X$ is a function $F(x)$ such that

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x).
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(6) & =P(X\le 6) \\  & =P(X\in {0,2,4,6}) \\  & =P(X=0)+P(X=2)+P(X=4)+P(X=6) \\  & =P(X\in {0,2,4})+P(X=6) \\  & =P(X\le 4)+P(X=6) \\  & =F(4)+P(X=6).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=6) & =F(6)-F(4) \\  & =\frac{7}{8}-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Computing a Probability Over an Interval Given the CDF
questions.problem:
Given that the discrete random variable $Y$ has the cumulative distribution function $F(y)$ shown in the table below, compute $P(\frac{1}{2}\le Y\le \frac{3}{2}).$

| $y$ | $0$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $1$ | $\frac{3}{2}$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $F(y)$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ | $0.4$ | $0.8$ | $1.0$ |
questions.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable $Y$ is a function $F(y)$ such that

$$
F(y)=P(Y\le y).
$$

To compute the probability of a random variable $Y$ over an interval, we can use the rule

$$
P(a<Y\le b)=F(b)-F(a).
$$

Here, we want to compute $P(\frac{1}{2}\le Y\le \frac{3}{2}).$ However, this interval is stated in the form $a\le Y\le b,$ not $a<Y\le b.$

So first, we must convert the interval $\frac{1}{2}\le Y\le \frac{3}{2}$ to the form $a<Y\le b.$ Looking at the given possible values of $Y,$ we see that $\frac{1}{2}\le Y$ is equivalent to $0<Y.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\frac{1}{2}\le Y\le \frac{3}{2}) & =P(0<Y\le \frac{3}{2}) \\  & =F(\frac{3}{2})-F(0) \\  & =0.8-0.1 \\  & =0.7.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that the discrete random variable $X$ has the cumulative distribution function $F(x)$ shown in the table below, compute $P(X\ge 6).$

| $x$ | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ | $8$ | $10$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $F(x)$ | $0.2$ | $0.3$ | $0.7$ | $0.8$ | $1.0$ |
questions.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable $X$ is a function $F(x)$ such that

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x).
$$

To solve the given problem, we can use the rule

$$
P(X>a)=1-P(X\le a)=1-F(a).
$$

Here, we want to compute $P(X\ge 6).$ However, this interval is stated in the form $X\ge 6,$ not $X>6.$

So first, we must convert the interval $X\ge 6$ to the form $X>a.$ Looking at the given possible values of $X,$ we see that $X\ge 6$ is equivalent to $X>4.$

Therefore, in our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 6) & =P(X>4) \\  & =1-P(X\le 4) \\  & =1-F(4) \\  & =1-0.3 \\  & =0.7.\end{aligned}
$$

The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable $T$ is a function $F(t)$ such that

$$
F(t)=P(T\le t).
$$

To solve the given problem, we can use the rule

$$
P(T>a)=1-P(T\le a)=1-F(a).
$$

Here, we want to compute $P(T\ge 2).$ However, this interval is stated in the form $T\ge 2,$ not $T>2.$

So first, we must convert the interval $T\ge 2$ to the form $T>a.$ Looking at the given possible values of $T,$ we see that $T\ge 2$ is equivalent to $T>\frac{3}{2}.$

Therefore, in our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(T\ge 2) & =P(T>\frac{3}{2}) \\  & =1-P(T\le \frac{3}{2}) \\  & =1-F(\frac{3}{2}) \\  & =1-\frac{1}{3} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Given that the discrete random variable $Y$ has the probability mass function $f(y),$ shown in the table below, and the cumulative distribution function $F(y),$ compute $F(2).$

| $y$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(y)$ | $\dfrac{1}{2}$ | $\dfrac{1}{8}$ | $\dfrac{1}{4}$ | $\dfrac{1}{8}$ |
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable $Y$ is the function $F(y)$ defined by

$$
F(y) = P(Y \leq y).
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(2) & =P(Y\le 2) \\  & =P(Y\in {1,2}) \\  & =P(Y=1)+P(Y=2) \\  & =f(1)+f(2) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{8} \\  & =\frac{5}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Given that the discrete random variable $X$ has the cumulative distribution function $F(x)$ shown in the table below, compute $P(X=5).$

| $x$ | $1$ | $3$ | $5$ | $7$ | $9$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $F(x)$ | $0.15$ | $0.45$ | $0.50$ | $0.90$ | $1.0$ |
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable $X$ is the function $F(x)$ defined by

$$
F(x) = P(X \leq x).
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(5) & =P(X\le 5) \\  & =P(X\in {1,3,5}) \\  & =P(X=1)+P(X=3)+P(X=5) \\  & =P(X\in {1,3})+P(X=5) \\  & =P(X\le 3)+P(X=5) \\  & =F(3)+P(X=5).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=5) & =F(5)-F(3) \\  & =0.50-0.45 \\  & =0.05.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Computing a Probability Over an Interval Given the CDF
canonical_examples.problem:
Given that the discrete random variable $Y$ has the cumulative distribution function $F(y)$ shown in the table below, compute $P\left( 2 \leq  Y <     5 \right).$

| $y$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ | $6$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $F(y)$ | $\dfrac{1}{4}$ | $\dfrac{1}{2}$ | $\dfrac{2}{3}$ | $\dfrac{3}{4}$ | $\dfrac{5}{6}$ | $1$ |
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable $Y$ is the function $F(y)$ defined by

$$
F(y) = P(Y \leq y).
$$

To compute the probability of a random variable $Y$ over an interval, we can use the rule

$$
P(a <            X \leq b) = F(b) - F(a).
$$

Here, we want to compute $P\left( 2 \leq  Y <     5 \right).$ However, this interval is stated in the form $a \leq  Y <    b,$ not $a <           Y \leq b.$

So first, we must convert the interval $2 \leq  Y <     5$ to the form $a <         X \leq b.$ Looking at the given possible values of $Y,$ we see that $2 \leq Y$ is equivalent to $1 <        Y,$ and  $Y<   5$ is equivalent to $Y \leq 4.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(2\le Y<5) & =P(1<Y\le 4) \\  & =F(4)-F(1) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}-\frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Given that the discrete random variable $X$ has the cumulative distribution function $F(x)$ shown in the table below, compute $P(X \gt 2).$

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $F(x)$ | $0.2$ | $0.6$ | $0.8$ | $0.9$ | $1.0$ |
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable $X$ is the function $F(x)$ defined by

$$
F(x) = P(X \leq x).
$$

To solve the given problem, we can use the rule

$$
P(X > a) = 1 - P(X\leq a) = 1-F(a).
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>2) & =1-P(X\le 2) \\  & =1-F(2) \\  & =1-0.6 \\  & =0.4.\end{aligned}
$$
